title: AutoFill and Flash Fill
summary: Series of numbers, dates and months; filling patterns; splitting names with Flash Fill.
objectives: Use the fill handle to copy values and continue series.
Set the step of a series with two starting cells.
Use Flash Fill (Ctrl+E) to split or join text by example.

p: The **fill handle** is the small square at the bottom-right of the selection. Drag it down or across and Excel continues what you started.
Excel recognises patterns: **Jan** becomes Feb, Mar…; **Monday** becomes Tuesday; **Week 1** becomes Week 2; a date moves on by a day. A single number like 5 is simply copied.
Select **two** cells to show the step: 1 and 2 continue as 3, 4, 5; 5 and 10 continue as 15, 20, 25; Jan and Mar continue as May, Jul.
**Double-click** the fill handle to fill down automatically as far as the column next to it has data. For a formula in a 5,000-row table, that’s one double-click.

visual.caption: Select 5 and 10, then drag the fill handle

check.q: You select a cell with 5 and a cell with 10, then drag the fill handle down two cells. What appears?
check.explain: Two cells set a step of 5, so the series continues 15, 20.

p: **Flash Fill** fills a column by copying a pattern you type once. Beside a column of full names, type the first name for the first row, then press **Ctrl+E** (or Data › Flash Fill). Excel fills the rest.
It works for splitting (first and last names, PIN codes from addresses), joining (first + last), and tidying (capitalising names).
Flash Fill guesses from your example, so look through the results, especially names with three words. If one is wrong, fix it and Excel learns from the correction.
The results are plain values, not formulas: they won’t update if the names change. When they must update, you’ll use text functions (C2).

visual.text: Flash Fill is in Excel on Windows and Mac. It isn’t in this app’s grid, so you’ll try it in the Real Excel task below.

check.q: You used Flash Fill to pull first names out of full names. Then a full name changes. What happens to its first name?
options: It stays as it was, because Flash Fill writes plain values
check.explain: Flash Fill results are values, not formulas.

real.title: Split names with Flash Fill
steps: Column A has ten full names. In **B2**, type the first name of A2: *Asha*.
Press **Ctrl+E** (or Data › Flash Fill). Check every result.
In **C2**, type the last name *Rao* and press Ctrl+E again.

points: The **fill handle** copies single values and continues series: months, days, dates, “Week 1”.
